leading hypothesisNot confirmed

The backend ignores a late Ended that arrives after the connector is already Available, leaving the session open. This mechanism is seen directly in one log.

Supports it

  • Stuck cases cluster on drops within 90 s of unplug, around the reconnect.

Day 20 · 14 days after the change shipped on day 6

Verification

When a charger reconnects while the backend holds an open transaction on it, the backend asks the charger (GetTransactionStatus) and keeps the transaction open while messages are queued. Events are keyed on the station, transactionId and seqNo, and applied once, in seqNo order, whatever the EVSE status. The backend closes a transaction provisionally, at its own last recorded meter value, only when the charger reports it is not ongoing with nothing queued, the event sequence has no gaps, and recorded energy is flat; the invoice is then marked provisional for billing review. Anything else (energy still rising, no ongoing report, a sequence gap, or a newer transaction on the same EVSE) goes to a person. A late Ended after a provisional close replaces the provisional values once and does not create a second charge.

Sessions stay open after unplug-time websocket drop

Draft by AIS2

14 tickets (5 open, 9 closed earlier as one-offs) across 9 sites and two firmware lines (FW-B 4.2.x, FW-A 3.9.0) in 21 days.

The ask

Decide whether to change session-svc to accept a late Ended after the connector is Available, and to approve the 15-minute detector until the fix ships. Also assign the FW-B 4.2.x capture test.

Why it crosses the escalation line

  • ✓Needs a code, firmware or production config change (fired)
  • ✓Same pattern at 3+ sites, or recurring for 2+ weeks (fired)
  • ✓Billing or session data correctness at risk (fired)
  • Any safety concern (did not fire)

Reproduce

  1. Run the lab reproduction test with the fix flag off: simulated charger unplugs, drops websocket, reconnects, reports Available, then sends queued Ended.
  2. The test passes by asserting the bug: session-svc ignores the Ended as out of order and the transaction stays open.
  3. This shows backend behaviour only. It says nothing about whether FW-B sends or queues its Ended after the drop.
  4. Manual step: on a FW-B 4.2.x test charger, drop the connection after EVCommunicationLost but before Ended is sent; capture at charger and gateway.

The reproduction test in the lab: StuckSessionReproductionTest (opens the repository in a new tab). It runs with the fix flag off and shows the session staying open.

Evidence attached

  • Lab tests: bug reproduced; regression fails without the fix
  • CP-022-04 log: late Ended ignored, connector already Available
  • CP-014-02 and CP-031-01 logs: Available after reconnect, no Ended
  • Fleet view: FW-B 4.2.x 12 of 19 stuck; 41 other drops, 0 stuck
  • Unplug-to-drop times for 14 stuck sessions, all 3 to 88 s

The attachments are in the Incident tab: the three gateway log excerpts, the fleet table and the unplug-to-drop timings. Linked tickets: T-2041T-2047T-2053T-2058T-2066H-1903H-1911H-1922H-1930H-1938H-1947H-1955H-1962H-1968

  • App display bug: unlikely, session API itself returns state=Charging
  • Single bad site or charger: unlikely, 14 tickets across 9 sites
  • Driver behaviour: unlikely, every connector reported Available within 2 minutes of unplug

Support corrected the 5 open sessions with RB-05 at last meter value and reversed idle fees; invoice flagged for billing review; a 15-minute detector query is proposed, not yet running.

How I'd run it · a proposal to adjust with the team

Eastern-hours dev support, day to day

The NOC covers the network around the clock and India engineering covers 23:30–08:30 ET. This shift covers 07:00–15:30 ET, so every day starts with ninety minutes of live overlap. The aim is that the India team's time goes to engineering: the Eastern-hours queue is handled here, and anything that needs them arrives as one complete packet.

The day

  1. 07:00–08:30

    Live handover with India engineering

    What is open, what changed overnight, what needs a decision. Anything they are mid-way through stays with its owner or is handed over by name.

  2. 08:30

    NOC sync

    Alerts and repeat offenders from the night: which chargers, which sites, which ones have been reset before. During the day the NOC reaches this shift directly, with an agreed time to acknowledge.

  3. Through the day

    Triage and investigate

    Runbook closures go to a person for approval. A symptom that keeps coming back is held and treated as a pattern. Anything past the escalation line becomes one incident with one owner and one packet for engineering. Customer updates on an incident have a named owner too.

  4. 15:30

    End-of-shift note to India

    Done, needs you (ticket ids, an owner and a deadline for each), escalated, watch.

When it goes to engineering

Proposed, not an existing policy.

Support owns it when

  • A runbook exists and fixes it
  • No code, firmware or production config change needed
  • One site or one charger

It goes to engineering when any of these hold

  • Needs a code, firmware or production config change
  • Same pattern at 3+ sites, or recurring for 2+ weeks
  • Billing or session data correctness at risk
  • Any safety concern

Boundaries

  • What this role may change on its own: runbook actions a person has approved. Anything that changes production configuration, billing or code goes through the owning team.
  • Evenings (15:30–23:30 ET): automation keeps triaging and the escalation line still applies; who is paged for an urgent billing or regional issue is agreed with engineering, not assumed.

What I'd measure

Measure first for a few weeks, then agree targets with the team.

  • Time from escalation to first engineering response.
  • Share of tickets closed by a runbook, and share that needed engineering.
  • Repeat symptoms per runbook after mitigation: a sign that a cause is still open.
  • Tickets reopened after closure.
  • Handoffs sent back for missing information, in either direction.

The first 90 days

First 30 days

  • Learn the platform, the runbooks and the ticketing tools the NOC and support teams use.
  • Join the India handovers and take the Eastern-hours queue with review.
  • Agree the escalation line and the handover note format with engineering and the NOC.
  • Start measuring, with no targets yet.
  • Write down the ten most common recurring symptoms and where each one ends up.

By 60 days

  • Own the Eastern-hours queue.
  • Review with their owners the runbooks that keep closing the same symptom.

By 90 days

  • Take one recurring pattern from tickets to an engineering fix, and verify it (against a control where that is possible).
  • Put numbers on the measures above, then agree targets with the team.

Engineering notes

How this was built, and what it does not prove

Built with AI coding assistants. I decided what to build and the rules it had to follow, reviewed the code, and checked it with tests and independent reviews by separate AI models. The assistants wrote much of the code.

The two parts

  • The desk

    React and TypeScript, Cloudflare Pages Functions, Vitest and Playwright with accessibility checks. Source

  • The reproduction lab

    Java 25, Spring Boot 4, PostgreSQL through Testcontainers, a scripted charger over a real websocket. Source

How the AI output is checked

  • Every triage decision quotes the ticket. A quote that is not in the ticket (ignoring case, spacing and punctuation) is rejected, and the rules answer instead.
  • A closure must name a real runbook and fit the ticket, and a person approves it. A record-only runbook also needs a person to confirm the meter first.
  • A record-only runbook that keeps closing the same symptom is held, and the tickets become a pattern.
  • Every AI answer shows its model, the checks that ran, and its cost. A rules answer is labelled as rules.

The validatorsThe cases they are tested against

What two rounds of AI review found, and what changed

FoundNow
Transactions were keyed on transactionId alone, but OCPP ids are only unique per charging station.Transactions and event idempotency are keyed on the station as well.
Events were replayed by timestamp, so a charger clock correction could reorder them.Events replay in seqNo order, counted from the transaction's own Started. A gap, or a missing Started, stops automatic reconciliation.
A charger that did not report ongoingIndicator was treated as not ongoing.Only an explicit not-ongoing answer, with nothing queued, allows a provisional close. Silence goes to a person; a charger that says ongoing is left alone.
Two equal meter samples were taken as proof the session had stopped.The samples must be a minimum time apart, recent, and not dated more than two minutes ahead of the backend clock. Otherwise a person decides.
An invoice could be confirmed from incomplete data: an Ended without a meter value, or a sequence with a gap.It stays provisional for review until the data is complete. The lab records one charge per transaction; it has no real payment system.
A newer transaction could start on the same charging point between the check and the close.Both paths take a per-charging-point lock in a fixed order, so the check sees it.
The reconciliation sweep ignored the per-station switch for the fix.It skips any station where the fix is turned off.

Each fix has a test that would have caught the original problem.

The same problem on OCPP 1.6

The lab models 2.0.1. On 1.6 an analogous race exists, with fewer tools to resolve it:

  • The backend assigns the transactionId, in StartTransaction.conf.
  • The protocol defines chronological delivery of transaction-related messages, but provides no transaction-event sequence number. Backend deduplication needs message-specific rules; the transactionId and timestamps alone are not enough.
  • There is no standard query for whether a StopTransaction is still queued. The charger must queue transaction-related messages while offline; failed submissions are retried under TransactionMessageAttempts and TransactionMessageRetryInterval, and after the configured failure limit the message should be discarded.
  • If the charger supports the RemoteTrigger profile, TriggerMessage can ask for a StatusNotification or MeterValues, but not for a StopTransaction.

OCPP 1.6 has no standard transaction-status query that returns an explicit not-ongoing answer. A 1.6 version of this fallback would combine waiting, connector status, meter evidence and a person; flat energy alone cannot establish that a transaction ended.

What the lab does not model

  • OCPP 1.6J itself (see above): the lab speaks 2.0.1 only.
  • TxStopPoint configuration, which decides when a charger ends a transaction.
  • Roaming (OCPI) and charge detail records.
  • Idle fees, real payment capture and refunds.
  • Production traffic volumes, or anything about a real company's systems. Every station, ticket and number is synthetic.

**Severity:** S2  
**Scope:** 14 tickets (5 open, 9 closed earlier as one-offs) across 9 sites and two firmware lines (FW-B 4.2.x, FW-A 3.9.0) in 21 days.

## The ask
Decide whether to change session-svc to accept a late Ended after the connector is Available, and to approve the 15-minute detector until the fix ships. Also assign the FW-B 4.2.x capture test.

## Reproduce

Support corrected the 5 open sessions with RB-05 at last meter value and reversed idle fees; invoice flagged for billing review; a 15-minute detector query is proposed, not yet running.
